summary: GitHub OAuth apps are created instantly in your account settings — no approval process. You get a client ID and secret immediately and can start testing right away.
difficultyReason: Creating an OAuth app is self-serve and instant for any account. There is no review step to use it; review only applies if you later want a GitHub App listed on the GitHub Marketplace.

time.approvalWait: None to create and use the app for any number of users
time.notes: Rate limits for OAuth apps are higher once a user has authorized, and GitHub may ask you to verify your app's identity only if you request certain org-level permissions.

whenReviewIsNeeded.text: No review is required to create or use a standard OAuth app, including for third-party users signing in.
Review/listing is only needed if you want to publish a GitHub App on the GitHub Marketplace.

requirements.text: A GitHub account (personal or organization) to register the app under.
A homepage URL and an authorization callback URL (redirect URI) for your app.

steps.title: Go to Developer settings
steps.detail: In GitHub, open Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps, then click 'New OAuth App'.

steps.title: Fill in app details
steps.detail: Provide an application name, homepage URL, and authorization callback URL. The callback URL must exactly match what your app sends during the OAuth flow.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: After registering, click 'Generate a new client secret'. Store the client ID and secret securely — the secret is shown only once.

steps.title: Implement the authorization flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to GitHub's authorize endpoint with your client ID and requested scopes, then exchange the returned code for an access token.

blockers.problem: Callback URL mismatch causes GitHub to reject the authorization request.
blockers.fix: Make sure the redirect_uri sent in your authorization request exactly matches the Authorization callback URL registered for the app (including path and trailing slashes).

agentCanDo: Draft the authorization URL and scope list
humanMustDo: Log into GitHub and register the OAuth app
Generate and securely store the client secret
openQuestions: Exact rate limit thresholds for OAuth apps depend on whether the user has authorized the app and whether you're on GitHub Enterprise; not independently verified here.
